summary: API gateway idle-timeout and header-size truncation resulting in intermittent 502/504s for streaming requests
sli_impact: increased tail latency for streaming endpoints; 502/504 spike observed between 2026-03-09T22:00Z and 2026-03-10T03:00Z
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports an uptick in failed streaming calls and end-user timeouts when hitting our Chat/stream endpoint. Error responses returned to clients are mostly 502 and occasional 504. Impact: multiple SynthRetail production customers experienced degraded chat sessions and some lost streaming partials leading to downstream UX issues and increased support load. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east, gateway fleet behind L7 load balancers, dedicated serving pool for customer.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Make long-polling streaming request to /v1/chat/stream using chunked transfer encoding and a large cookie+auth header set from SynthRetail SDK.
2) Observe HTTP response code or abrupt connection termination after ~60s idle period.
3) Repeat under moderate QPS (~15rps per connection) to reproduce intermittent failures.

Observed behavior: Streaming connections drop with 502 Bad Gateway or 504 Gateway Timeout. Relevant gateway logs show connection closed with reason "upstream reset" and sometimes "header too large" warnings. Metrics show a correlated increase in proxy 502/504s and an increase in per-connection idle timeout hits after a deployment on 2026-03-09.

Expected behavior: Long-lived streaming connections should remain open for the whole stream duration (many >2 minutes) unless explicitly terminated by server or client. Gateways should not truncate large headers or close on idle when a stream has recent payloads.

Logs/attachments:
- customer supplied curl transcript and SDK logs (attached)
- gateway logs slice: https://logs.redwood/streams/SUP-11208/gateway-2026-03-10.txt
- datadog dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/redwood/streaming-gateway-502s

Workaround: Advised customer to reduce cookie size and remove non-essential headers; temporary increase of keepalive probe on edge LB for their pool applied as stopgap.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after CS call with SynthRetail. Customer observed spike starting after our control-plane config roll on 2026-03-09 21:45Z.

2026-03-10 - Diego Morales: Acknowledged. Initial hypothesis: recent gateway config change lowered idle timeout and applied proxy_buffering toggles. Kicking off quick config diff against previous rollout.

2026-03-10 - SRE (Liu Chen): Found matching deploy (routing-config v1.14.3) with change to nginx proxy_buffering = on and proxy_read_timeout set from 300s to 60s for L7 pool. Also saw header-buffer-size reduce from 16k to 8k in template. Adding to investigation notes.
2026-03-11 - Diego Morales: Applied temporary override to increase proxy_read_timeout to 240s for SynthRetail dedicated pool. Monitoring for 24h.

2026-03-12 - SynthRetail support contact (Maria Gomez): Reported improvement; seen far fewer disconnects but some clients still hit header size errors when using legacy SDK. Requested permanent config change and a recomendation for SDK header trimming.
2026-03-12 - Diego Morales: Marking workaround in place; planning permanent fix in routing-config PR and coordination with SDK team for header size guidance.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 22:10Z: Retrieved deploy history and diff. Change introduced in routing-config PR 578 reduced default proxy header buffers and set proxy_buffering on by default to improve upstream throughput.

2026-03-10 22:35Z: Correlated spike window with the rollout. Datadog trace shows upstream read stalls at ~58s leading to connection reset; also saw 'client sent too large header' warnings in some LB nodes.

2026-03-10 23:02Z: Reproduced locally by sending large authorization cookie + long-lived chunked stream: after 60s of inactivity on a particular connection (no client chunk), LB closed idle connection. However some SDKs send keepalives less frequently than heartbeat interval leading to idle closure.

2026-03-11 01:15Z: Confirmed proxy_buffering enabled changes the read behavior: when buffering is enabled and upstream doesn't flush frequently, some proxies consider the connection idle and hit lower read timeout.

2026-03-11 04:00Z: Temporary override applied: proxy_read_timeout increased to 240s and large_client_header_buffers increased back to 16k for the dedicated pool. Early metrics show 85% reduction in 502s for affected pool.
Next steps: run a full config audit for other dedicated pools, propose routing-config rollback for default values or make values pool-specific, and coordinate SDK advisory for header sizes.
resolution: Temporary workaround: proxy_read_timeout increased and large_client_header_buffers restored for SynthRetail pool on 2026-03-11 02:45Z. Monitoring indicates reduced error rate.

Permanent fix: Created routing-config PR 582 to add pool-scoped timeout and header buffer overrides and to disable proxy_buffering for streaming endpoints by default. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-config/pull/582
SDK guidance: Created internal ticket INT-4123 for Developer Experience to publish header-size best practices and to add automatic header trimming in the JavaScript/Node SDK.

Postmortem: Assigning postmortem to SRE and Edge teams; draft due 2026-03-19. Action items include: config QA checklist for rollout, perf test for streaming endpoints, and alerts for sudden proxy config changes.

Customer communication: Sent summary and mitigation steps to SynthRetail on 2026-03-12; included rollback plan and timeline for permanent fix. Customer satisfied with temporary mitigation and awaiting PR merge.
follow_up_tasks: INT-4124: Add automated pre-deploy check to detect lowering of large_client_header_buffers or proxy_read_timeout below streaming-safe thresholds.
INT-4125: Add Datadog monitor to alert on sudden increase in 'client sent too large header' and 502 spikes per pool.
INT-4123: (linked) SDK header trimming work for Node and Python SDKs.
SRE-POSTMORTEM-11208: Runbook update and learnings doc to be authored.
